cards.name: wave-cooperative-register-top-k-plus-radix-seeded-threshold-knn-search-gfx942-both
cards.description: Brute-force 3-D kNN: wave-cooperative register top-k in one native-layout dispatch, then a radix-select threshold seed: ~54x geomean on gfx942
cards.key: Brute-force point-cloud k-nearest-neighbour (3-D fp32, small k) HIP kernel behind a PyTorch extension · gfx942/MI308X · standard, transposed and self-query call paths
cards.effect: ~54x geomean director-verified vs frozen baseline, non-overlapping, oracle index parity on 5 shapes x 3 call paths; per-case 12-14x on the smallest (host-floored) shape, 36-88x on self-query, 45-250x on the mid/large standard and transposed cases
cards.roofline: latency-bound (serial per-thread N loop, scratch-spilled top-k, multi-dispatch, ~0.78 of wave cycles in dependency wait) -> host-floored on tiny shapes, latency/under-fill on mid shapes, VALU+vL1 co-limited on self-query at ~0.4-0.45 VALU and TA busy; HBM/L2 not a lever
cards.title: Register top-k in one wave, one dispatch, then seed the threshold with a radix-select
cards.lever: Give each query to a whole wave: lanes stride N, keep the top-k in registers (no scratch), stage refs via LDS, read both input layouts natively and write the int32 index output directly. Then seed the k-th-distance threshold with a radix-select over the first chunk so later tiles insert only a handful of candidates.
cards.apply: One pybind entry -> one kernel launch per call (no dist2 buffer, fill, transposes or casts). Non-negative fp32 distances order like uint32, so threshold/radix logic runs as integer compares in SGPRs; use SGPR-offset buffer loads and packed fp32 distance math to cut VALU per pair ~3x.
cards.stack:
total ~54x geomean (director-verified) = two rounds, each an integrated merge
  - 1. wave-cooperative register top-k (round 1, verified 7.7x alone) + single-dispatch host entry (1.06x alone) -> 31.3x only when hand-merged into one launcher; stacked unchanged they gave 17.1x
  - 2. radix-select threshold seed + packed fp32 + SGPR addressing (round 2, 1.38x over round 1) and a lean builtin host fast path (~1.08x over round 1) -> 1.73x over round 1 together (disjoint files, unchanged launcher signature)
  - note: attribution is incremental in landing order; host gains only surface once the kernel stops dominating.
cards.verify: Frozen-baseline A/B per shape and call path plus exact index parity vs a cdist+topk reference; confirm scratch is zero, dispatch count is one, and VALU per pair dropped (counter pass) before crediting the seed.
cards.pitfall:
Two verified patches stacked unchanged reached about half the hand-merged speedup -> the host entry still reached the old multi-dispatch launcher -> merge so the new kernel is reached through the single-dispatch entry.
A patch into the gitignored workspace silently did nothing -> git apply skips files under ignored paths without an error -> apply with patch -p1 and confirm the edits landed.
HIP-graph replay lost on every case -> a single-dispatch op has no launch chain to amortize and replay costs about a bare launch -> measure the empty-graph replay floor first.
Multiple queries per wave regressed -> doubled live VGPRs to save loads that already hit L2/vL1 -> keep one query per wave unless VGPRs stay low.
cards.caution: Also verify where per-wave time goes (an s_memtime phase probe) before tuning insertion further - after the seed, load+distance dominated insertion roughly 2:1; and check fill on mid shapes, where too few waves each walk many tiles serially.
